paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Blessing the LORD starts with remembering. David tells his own soul, "do not forget all His kind deeds" (Psalm 103:2). Your soul is a LEAKY bucket, friend, and mine too. Good things go in, and by Tuesday we're asking, "Has anything good ever happened to me?"

So what does David remind himself of? He says the LORD is "compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion" (Psalm 103:8). He says the LORD "has not dealt with us according to our sins or repaid us according to our iniquities" (Psalm 103:10). And as far as the east is from the west, that's how far He has removed our transgressions from us (Psalm 103:12). He knows our frame, and He is mindful that we are dust (Psalm 103:14). He's not shocked by how small we are. I think that's the best news in the whole psalm.

Our days are like grass, but the loving devotion of the LORD goes "from everlasting to everlasting" to those who fear Him (Psalm 103:17). His kingdom rules over all (Psalm 103:19), so the praise gets BIG, from angels to every work in all places of His dominion. And then David turns right back to his own soul, because the praise starts at home. So today, baker, do what David did. Name one kind deed out loud, and then tell your soul to bless the LORD. I tell my mustache the same thing, and it does NOT always listen.
